title: Greetings, Konbini Survival & Everyday Politeness
subtitle: Time-of-day greetings, convenience store checkout decoding, essential signage, and polite social cushioning
summary: Step off the plane and walk straight into a Japanese konbini with calm confidence. Master core greetings, versatile survival responses like すみません and 大丈夫です, storefront Kanji signs, polite です/ます requests, casual neighborhood small talk, and full service-level Keigo.
communicativeCanDo: Greet staff, hosts, and locals naturally across morning, afternoon, and evening contexts
Decode rapid-fire konbini register questions about bags, warming bento, point cards, and contactless payment
Read core storefront signage (入口, 出口, 営業中) and ask polite location or checkout questions
Shift smoothly from survival phrases to casual neighborhood rapport and formal Keigo cushion expressions
culturalInsight: Japan's ~56,000 convenience stores (コンビニ) are civic infrastructure: you can grab freshly steamed hot food, withdraw yen from international ATMs, ship luggage, and pay bills 24/7. Clerks speak in rapid, elevated service Japanese (接客用語), yet as a customer you only need two calm, warm responses—「はい、お願いします」 (Yes, please) and 「大丈夫です」 (I'm fine / No, thank you)—paired with a slight nod.
